The headlines
BGP wins assembly polls for Rajinagar and Nandigram constituencies in West Bengal.
In Tamil Nadu ruling TVK wins assembly by polls for Maduran Takam and Dharapuram seats.
All India NR Congress retains Dhatan Chowri assembly constituency in Puducherry.
BGP also bags Assam's Nagav Lok Sabha seat.

The BJP has registered massive victories in both assembly constituencies of West Bengal,
Nandigram and East Mednipur district, and Reji Nagar and Murshidabad district, whereby
elections were held.
In Nandigram, BJP candidate Hasi Rani Rath defeated a nearest rival, Congress candidate
Melan Pradhan, by a margin of over 1,22,000 votes.

Assembly constituency by election. The seat was vacated by Puducherry Chief Minister,
Ayan Drangasamy. In Tamil Nadu, the ruling Tamilagavetri Karagam TVK has won the Assembly
Bipoles for Madhuran Takam and Dharapuram seats today. In Madhuran Takam TVK candidate
K. Maragatham Kumarvel defeated DMK's I. Paranthaman by 73,801 votes. The DMK candidate secured
53,743 votes. In Dharapuram TVK candidate P. Satyabhama won the seat by securing 66,841
votes against DMK candidate as Suganya, who got 57,370 votes, with a difference of 9,471
votes.
In Assam, BJP candidate Devashi Sharma has emerged victorious in the Nogau Lok Sabha
by election.
Mr. Sharma defeated A.I.U.D.F. Chief Badudrin Ajman by a comfortable margin of over 140,000
votes.
Congress finished third.

Prime Minister Nandar Modi has said that the looks of a result of Nogau in Assam and assembly results in Nondigram as well as Rajinagar in West Bengal show yet again that the people have a deep-rooted connect with the good governance agenda of the BJP NDA.
In a social media post, Mr. Modi congratulated the victorious BJP candidates and also applauded the hard work of party workers.
He also congratulated N-D-A-L-I, A-I-N-R-C for the win in Thatanand Chowdi in Puducherry.
Senior BJP Leader and Home Minister Mit Shah said the N-D-A-S victories in the by-elections
in West Bengal, Assam and Puducherry and the recently held local body polls in Rajasthan
and Tripura demonstrated that the people have completely rejected the INDI Alliance.
This is Akash Vani giving you the news.

Delhi Police has denied permission for the proposed protests by the CJP at Jantar Mantar
tomorrow. Addressing the media in New Delhi today, Delhi Police Joint Commissioner Nupur
Prasad said that applications seeking permission to hold protests to other programs at Jantar
Mantar must be submitted at least 10 days in advance. Ms Prasad noted that the CJP
had previously been granted permission to hold a protest at the venue, but failed to comply
with the prescribed guidelines and the undertakings given by the party.
The Joint Commission has said the decision to deny permission was taken in view of the
prevailing law and order situation, public safety and traffic regulations in the New
Delhi area.
We have received an application from Syro Das Group and winner of Kokto Chanta Party.
The application is regarding an intimation for protest on 10th of October at Jantar Mantar.
The protest was regarding accountability of CEC.
This intimation was considered and it was found that the intimation was given a very short span of time,
whereas as per the prescribed guideline the intimation has to be received 10 days prior by protest which is planned.
Ms. Prasad further stated that prohibitory orders under Section 163 of the Bharatya Nagarig
Suraksha Sahita are currently in force in the area imposing necessary restrictions to
maintain public safety and law and order.
The Joint Commissioner warned that the Delhi Police would take appropriate legal action
against anyone found violating the law.
Meanwhile, due to security reasons, the entry and exit facility will remain closed
that 57 metro stations from 9 p.m. till tomorrow till further notice. However interchange facility
will remain available at all the concerned metro stations except New Delhi metro station.
These metro stations include Rajiv Chowk, Seva Tirth, Lok Kalyanmarg, Central Secretariat,
Janpat, Patel Chowk, New Delhi, Mandi House and Janpat. Earlier Delhi police had proposed
closure of the entry and exit gates of 57 metro stations from 9 p.m. tonight in view of the proposed
protest at Jantan Mantar in New Delhi tomorrow. Meanwhile, Namo Bharat train services between
Saray Kale Khan and New Ashok Nagar, Namo Bharat stations in Delhi will remain closed from 9 p.m.
tonight till 10 p.m. tomorrow. During this period, Namo Bharat train services between Anand Bihar
station in Delhi and Modi Puram station in UP, stations will continue to operate as per
schedule. Passengers have been requested to plan their journeys accordingly.
Meanwhile, DCP Railway B Bharat Reddy said special deployment arrangements of GRP personnel
have been made to maintain law and order in Delhi.
A special deployment has been made to maintain law and order in view of CGP's protest
call in Delhi tomorrow. Around the clock security personnel have been deployed at
all seven major railway stations in the national capital. A total of 334 GRP personnel including
around 120 women police personnel have been deployed. The authorities have also sought
additional forces from the Central Armed Police Force.
Furthermore in view of the law and order situation, Delhi Traffic Police has also issued an advisory
for traffic diversion in various parts of the national capital. It said that diversions
will come into force from 6 a.m. in the morning tomorrow, depending upon the prevailing situation.
All mail-in express trains departing from the source stations after 2 p.m. to there, and
scheduled to arrive at New Delhi and Hazrat Nizamuddin railway stations between 4 a.m.
and 2 p.m. tomorrow will be cancelled at source. The Railways Ministry said that this decision
has been taken in view of the anticipated severe road traffic congestion in areas around
both the railway stations tomorrow.
The Supreme Court has directed the sentin authorities to ensure that there is no complete suspension
of Delhi Metro and Railway services in the national capital in view of the CJP protest
scheduled for tomorrow.
A bench headed by Chief Justice of India, Surya Khan, said public transport services
must continue in a regulated manner to minimize inconvenience to commuters.

India today stressed that the steps announced by the US regarding Permanent Labour Certification
P-E-R-M program do not advance the shared ambitions of both countries.
Addressing me to New Delhi this afternoon, external affairs mystery spokesperson Randhir
Jaiswal emphasized that talent mobility adds value to both economies of India and the US.
Talent mobility adds value to both economies, that is economies of India and the United States.
While it creates opportunities for Indians, it equally helps US companies with cutting-edge talent, innovation,
research, productivity, competitiveness, and job creation besides creating shareholder
wealth in the United States.
This is therefore an area of tremendous mutual benefit for the two countries.
Mr. Jaiswal clarified that the US government's suspension of certain companies from the
PERM program does not by itself affect the validity of existing age 1B visas or
the status of visa holders and the dependents.
We are aware of the U.S. Department of Labor's decision concerning the Permanent Labor Certification
